chapter_title: Concerning the Four Archetypes that occur in the Eye, and the Fifth that is hidden in them; to whom do they belong?
chapter_note: Highly fragmentary, but dominated by cosmological-correspondential teaching: elemental/cosmic attributions (Fire, Darkness/abyss, Light/living air) and a microcosm teaching on the eye/pupil tied to cosmic structure (cardinal points; First Man). Paragraphs 1 and 3 carry a light hagiographic dialogue frame (“Once again he speaks:”) and explanatory address that likely entered with the compilation frame, but the underlying exposition remains internal to the cosmic system (cosmos↔man correspondences) rather than institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: There are four aspects among mankind that perceive, as they perceive [...] without these four that are hidden in them [...] they belong [...]. So, [...].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he speaks:” (formulaic Kephalaia wrapper).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening formula is a classic hagiographic/frame marker; the remaining fragment is a microcosm teaching (four perceiving aspects + a hidden element) stated as ontology rather than exhortation, consistent with the core layer despite lacunae.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] that is in the [...] belongs to the fire. The Darkness belongs to the abyss; but the Light that perceives what is hidden in all these things, being clear, is the living air.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, correspondential mapping of perceptual principles to cosmic elements (Fire / Darkness-abyss / Light-living air) with no citation, no exhortation, and no reach into contemporary institutions—typical substrate style.

paragraphs.core_text: How shall the pupil of the eye perceive? While it perceives by day, yet come the night it shall not perceive. What mystery does this matter signify? [...] The pupil of the eye shall not [...] the mystery of the [...] is the door [...] below [...] the other four cardinal points. For in the [...] above. He has [...] great [...] they came down [...] living [...]. The First Man came forth from it and knew all things.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he speaks:”. Removed explanatory address/application voice: “Look, I am the one who will explain to you what you do not know [...]”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula plus first-person didactic address suggests compilation framing; underneath is a structured cosmological explanation (eye/pupil as mystery ‘door’, relation to four cardinal points, descent, emergence of First Man) that stays within the cosmic architecture and reads like older systematic teaching.
